analysis_notes.full_gap_analysis: Torah #248 is a one-paragraph teaching (Likutay Moharan I, #248). The source text contains no explicit bechina language (no 'בְּחִינַת', no 'נִקְרָא' used as a parallel-aspects marker, no 'הוּא בְּחִינַת'). The single edge in the dataset for reference 248 is edge id 2282, correctly typed as 'eitza': 'סִפּוּרִים מִצַּדִּיקִים' causes/produces 'נִתְעוֹרֵר וְנִתְלַהֵב הַלֵּב בְּהִתְעוֹרְרוּת גָּדוֹל לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ'. The relationship described is strictly causal: stories of tzaddikim awaken the heart's desire for God because the tzaddik's reshimu (spiritual impression/trace) is reactivated through the telling. This is one concept producing a result in another, not two expressions of the same underlying reality. No bechina-typed edges exist or are missing for this Torah. No packages can be formed, and there are no orphaned nodes and no missing bechina concepts to add.
analysis_notes.note_on_reshimu: The word 'רְשִׁימוּ' (reshimu = impression/trace left by the tzaddik's service) appears as an explanatory bridge in the proof text. It could theoretically be extracted as a node that mediates the causal chain (stories → reshimu → arousal). However, the text presents it in a purely explanatory/causal role ('כִּי הָרְשִׁימוּ... זֹאת הָרְשִׁימוּ נִתְעוֹרֶרֶת... וְהִיא מְעוֹרֶרֶת'), not as a bechina-parallel of another concept. It does not belong in a bechina package.
